root.name: Vienna Game: Hamppe-Muzio Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3 g5 5. Bc4 g4 6. O-O

overview: In the Vienna Gambit White plays 3.f4 exf4 4.Nf3 g5 5.Bc4 g4 6.O-O, offering a knight for a ferocious attack. After 6...gxf3 7.Qxf3 White has two pawns' worth of compensation against the f7 square, but Black can survive. The line is a rare Muzio-style sacrifice.

white_ideas.idea: Sacrifice the knight for a strong attack
Attack f7 with the queen and bishop
Open lines with Nd5 and d4

black_ideas.idea: Take the piece with ...gxf3 and defend f7
Bring the queen back to the kingside

typical_structures.structure: Open kingside with White a piece down

character.notes: Sharp, with White sacrificing for the attack.

gambit.notes: White gives a piece and Black can keep it.

character.reason: A piece sacrifice for the attack in an open position.

gambit.reason: White gives up a knight and pawns for the attack and Black can keep the piece.

soundness.reason: With accurate defence the attack is thought to fall short.

structure.reason: The centre and kingside open with the f-file in play.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play the Muzio structures.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner and success depends on knowing the attack.

plans.reason: White sacrifices material to aim everything at f7 and the king.
